title: USMCA/CUSMA annual joint review — the first of the yearly cycle the US triggered by declining to extend
source: EST: an OUTER BOUND derived from the treaty's annual cadence, not a published meeting date and NOT an anniversary rule. Primary text read direct this session (2026-09-09), USMCA/CUSMA art. 34.7 at international.gc.ca .../cusma-aceum/text-texte/34.aspx (HTTP 200): art. 34.7.2 fixes the SIX-YEAR review 'On the sixth anniversary of the entry into force' (2020-07-01 -> 2026-07-01), but art. 34.7.4 says only that where a Party does not confirm extension 'the Commission shall meet to conduct a joint review EVERY YEAR for the remainder of the term' — it carries no anniversary, no month and no day. So the treaty fixes the CADENCE, not the DATE, and 2027-07-01 is the one-year-from-2026-07-01 deadline, the conservative anchor, not a scheduled meeting. The trigger is primary-sourced: USTR press release of 2026-07 (ustr.gov .../ambassador-greer-issues-statement-usmca-joint-review, fetched direct 2026-09-09, HTTP 200) — 'The United States did not agree to renew the USMCA in its current form. As a result, the USMCA is not renewed.' The YEAR is corroborated independently ('the Agreement will instead shift to annual reviews starting in 2027'). The IMPLEMENTING STATUTE was read verbatim at uscode.house.gov (19 U.S.C. 4611, HTTP 200): (b)(1) 'At least 270 days before a joint review commences' USTR must publish a Federal Register notice and hold a public hearing, and (e)(1) defines 'joint review' as any art. 34.7 review relating to extension — while (b)(2)'s 180-day report is expressly limited to 'a 6-year joint review'. (c)(1) attaches a 70-day-prior report to 'any subsequent annual joint review meeting'. No published 2027 meeting date exists in any source fetched this session
notes: ESTIMATE IN THE STRONG SENSE — IT WIDENS CAUTION AND LICENSES NO DATE-KEYED ACTION. The date's weakness is sharper than the proposal that filed it assumed: the proposal argued the day was 'derived' but the month 'well supported by the anniversary rule'. Reading art. 34.7 verbatim refutes that — the anniversary rule lives in 34.7.2 and governs the six-year review only; 34.7.4's annual reviews carry no date language at all, so the Free Trade Commission sets the day and nothing constrains it to July. Read 2027-07-01 as the outer bound of a twelve-month window opened 2026-07-01, not as a scheduled event. THE OBSERVABLE THAT WOULD RESOLVE IT is the 19 U.S.C. 4611(b)(1) Federal Register notice: for the 2026-07-01 review USTR published it 2025-09-17 (FR 2025-18010, 287 days out, 17 days inside the 270-day floor), comments closed 2025-11-03, hearing held 2025-12-03..05 at the USITC. On the same reading, a 2027-07-01 review needs its notice by 2026-10-04. As of 2026-09-09 NO such notice exists — verified mechanically against the Federal Register API filtered to USTR, which returns only Section 301 and procurement-threshold documents for all of 2026. That notice, whenever it lands, will name the review date and is the single event that converts this entry from derived to read. The 70-day art. 34.7 consultation date (~2027-04-22) is deliberately NOT proposed as its own calendar entry: it would be a derivation stacked on a derivation, the same refusal the proposing lane made. MEASURED MARKET CHANNEL, NIL: on 2026-07-01 — the first joint review in the agreement's history, at which the US refused to renew ~US$1.8T of North American trade terms — S&P 500 7499.36 -> 7483.23 (-0.22%), VIX 16.45 -> 16.59 (+0.14), USD/CAD 1.4205 -> 1.4205 (unchanged to four decimals), USD/MXN 17.4490 -> 17.5261 (peso -0.44%) and every one of those round-tripped by 2026-07-02 (SPX 7483.24, VIX 16.15, USD/CAD 1.4182, USD/MXN 17.4524). All readings from FRED (SP500, VIXCLS, DEXCAUS, DEXMXUS), fetched direct 2026-09-09. Filed medium, unchanged from the proposal: the review changes no obligation by itself, all USMCA rights stay operative through it, and the 2026 edition is measured at nil. Ledger: docs/research/events/usmca-joint-review-2027-07-01.md. Canonical file written 2026-09-09 by the never-assessed initial research, from proposals/usmca-joint-review-2027-07-01.from-canada-counter-tariffs-effective-2026-09-08.json plus the primary sources above; that proposal is now shadowed.
